mainTopic: Whose view the משנה on a refused נזיר follows; undoing a vow uproots הקדש; mistaken versus deliberate labeling in מעשר בהמה
overview: This amud opens with the last words of the משנה about counting animals for מעשר בהמה. The גמרא asks whose view the משנה follows when it lets a נזיר count from the day he vowed. A ברייתא shows the רבנן and רבי יוסי arguing about a נזיר who broke his vow, and at first the משנה seems to fit neither. The גמרא answers that it can fit רבי יוסי if it is about a short נזירות, or the רבנן if we read 'like from the time he vowed'. Next, רבי ירמיה shows that when a חכם undoes a נזיר's vow, both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree his animal goes back to the flock. The גמרא then brings a dispute between רב נחמן and רב חסדא with רבה בר רב הונא: does calling the wrong animal 'tenth' on purpose make it holy? רבא challenges רב נחמן, רב שימי בר אשי defends him with a קל וחומר, and the גמרא rejects that קל וחומר because הקדש depends on the owner's intention. Finally, a new משנה begins about a נזיר whose animal was stolen.

steps.title: The last words of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends its list of animals with the eleventh.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the closing words of the משנה, finishing its point about the animals that become holy in מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is just the end of a sentence that began earlier in the משנה. The real new discussion starts in the next step, when the גמרא begins.

keyTerms.meaning: Eleventh (here, the eleventh animal counted)

phrases.english: And the eleventh.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the משנה on the previous page about counting animals for מעשר בהמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continuation of the משנה from the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The holiness also takes effect on the eleventh animal.

steps.title: Whose view does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the משנה follows and answers that it seems to match neither רבי יוסי nor the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Whose view is our משנה? It is neither רבי יוסי nor the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who wrote the rule in the משנה that a person counts his נזירות from the moment he vowed. It answers right away that the rule does not seem to fit either side of a known argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if a חכם refused to cancel the vow, the person counts from the day he vowed, even the days he did not act like a נזיר. The גמרא is setting up a problem: it will show that this rule clashes with both opinions in a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Whose view is our משנה?
The Sages (the majority view)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Neither רבי יוסי nor the רבנן' is not the end of the discussion. It is a problem the גמרא will now try to solve.

phrases.english: גמרא: Whose view is our משנה?
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's rule that a נזיר whose request was refused counts from the day he made the vow.

phrases.english: Not רבי יוסי and not the רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא agrees with the משנה's rule of counting from the time of the vow?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It appears to match neither רבי יוסי nor the רבנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא about a נזיר who broke his vow
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a נזיר who broke his vow must make up the days he broke it, while רבי יוסי says thirty days is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Someone who vowed to be a נזיר and broke his נזירות is not attended to unless he keeps the prohibitions for as many days as he acted as if things were permitted. רבי יוסי says: thirty days is enough for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that shows the two opinions, the רבנן and רבי יוסי. This is the source for the claim it just made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say the days he broke the vow do not count, so he must add the same number of days. רבי יוסי is more lenient: thirty days is enough, so extra days are needed only in a longer case. The next step shows how each view clashes with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
The state of being a נזיר
We do not deal with him (we don't handle his request or let him finish)
It is enough for him

phrases.english: As it is taught:
One who vowed and transgressed his נזירות,
we do not attend to him,
phrases.notes: The חכמים won't take up his request to cancel the vow or let him finish with his קרבנות.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מוֹנֶה בָּהֶן אִיסּוּר
phrases.english: unless he counts days of prohibition
like the days in which he acted with permission.
רבי יוסי says:
Thirty days is enough for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind the claim that the משנה matches neither view
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה follows neither רבי יוסי nor the רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where the רבנן require making up all broken days, and רבי יוסי caps it at thirty

steps.title: Each view clashes with the משנה in a different case
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is the רבנן's, a short נזירות is a problem. If it is רבי יוסי's, a long נזירות is a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is the רבנן, a short נזירות is difficult. If it is רבי יוסי, a long נזירות is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly why the משנה cannot be either opinion. Each one breaks down in a different kind of נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן always require making up broken days, even in a short thirty-day נזירות, but the משנה lets him count from the vow. רבי יוסי may fit a short נזירות, but in a long נזירות even he requires extra days, while the משנה requires none.

keyTerms.meaning: If
It is difficult
A short נזירות (the regular thirty days)
A long נזירות (longer than thirty days)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's rule of counting from the time of the vow fails with the רבנן for a short נזירות, and with רבי יוסי for a long one. So it seems to fit neither.

phrases.english: If it is the רבנן,
a short נזירות is difficult.
phrases.notes: Even in a regular thirty-day נזירות, the רבנן make him add the days he broke it.

phrases.english: If it is רבי יוסי,
a long נזירות is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא to spell out why the משנה clashes with both opinions
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the משנה follows either the רבנן or רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה counts broken days without adding any. The רבנן add days even in a short נזירות, and רבי יוסי adds days in a long נזירות, so neither matches the משנה in every case.

steps.title: The משנה can fit רבי יוסי: long versus short נזירות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה can fit either opinion. For רבי יוסי, the ברייתא is about a long נזירות and the משנה is about a short one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say the משנה follows רבי יוסי, and if you want, say it follows the רבנן. If you want to say רבי יוסי: here the ruling is about a long נזירות, and there the ruling is about a short נזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from step 4. It first says the משנה can fit both sides, then shows how it fits רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוסי, extra days are required only in a long נזירות, which is the case of the ברייתא. The משנה is speaking of a short נזירות, where even רבי יוסי requires no added days, so counting from the time he vowed fits. The two sources are talking about different cases and do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, you can say. It brings an answer, often one of two possible answers
Here... there. It splits two sources into two different cases
A long נזירות, more than thirty days
A short נזירות

phrases.english: If you wish, say it is Rabbi Yosei,
and if you wish, say it is the Rabbis.
If you wish, say it is Rabbi Yosei:
here it is about a long naziriteship,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the ברייתא, where רבי יוסי says thirty days is enough.

phrases.english: there it is about a short naziriteship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, וְאִיבָּעֵית תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 4 about matching the משנה to רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): long נזירות versus short נזירות
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'from the time he vowed' seemed to go against רבי יוסי's thirty-day limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוסי's limit is for a long נזירות. The משנה is about a short נזירות, so the two fit together.

steps.title: The משנה can fit the רבנן if we read 'like from the time he vowed'
steps.stepSummary: For the רבנן, the גמרא reads the משנה's wording slightly differently: not 'from the time he vowed' but 'like the time since he vowed'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it follows the רבנן: do not say 'from the time that he vowed', but say 'like from the time that he vowed'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second answer, showing how the משנה fits the רבנן by changing how we read one phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From the time he vowed' sounds like the days since the vow, including the days he broke it, already count toward his נזירות. 'Like from the time he vowed' means he must keep a number of days equal to the time that has passed since his vow. That matches the רבנן, who say the broken days must be made up.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not say... rather say. The גמרא changes how a phrase should be read
Like from the time he vowed, meaning an amount of time equal to it

steps.confusionAlert: The only difference is the one letter כ. Without it, the days since his vow count toward his נזירות, even the broken ones. With it, he must keep a number of days equal to the time since his vow, so the broken days are made up.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה works for both sides. For רבי יוסי it is about a short נזירות. For the רבנן we read 'like from the time he vowed', meaning he makes up the days he broke.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say it is the Rabbis:
do not say 'from the time that he vowed',
rather say 'like from the time that he vowed'.
phrases.notes: He makes up as many days as passed since his vow, which is just what the רבנן said.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן: לָא תֵּימָא מִשָּׁעָה שֶׁנָּזַר, אֶלָּא אֵימָא כְּמִשָּׁעָה שֶׁנָּזַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second way to answer the same problem, this time matching the משנה to the רבנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'From the time he vowed' seemed to mean the days since the vow count toward his נזירות, even the broken ones, which goes against the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it as 'like from the time he vowed', meaning he makes up the days that passed, which matches the רבנן.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: we can learn בית הלל's view from בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about a נזיר whose vow was undone by the חכמים. רבי ירמיה says we can learn what בית הלל hold from what בית שמאי hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he asked the חכמים and they undid his vow, his animal goes out to the flock. רבי ירמיה said: from בית שמאי we can learn about בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה. רבי ירמיה states his main claim here, and the next steps prove and explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a נזיר who set aside an animal for his offering, and then a חכם undid his vow. רבי ירמיה wants to show that בית הלל agree the animal is not holy, and he will prove it from בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked the חכמים to undo his vow
They undid his vow, so it is as if it never existed
We can learn

phrases.english: He asked the Sages and they dissolved it for him, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. It goes on to say the animal he set aside goes out to graze in the flock.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
From Beit Shammai we can learn about Beit Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׁאַל לַחֲכָמִים וְהִתִּירוּהוּ וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: מִדְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי נִשְׁמַע לִדְבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: What בית הלל hold about the animal of a נזיר whose vow was undone can be learned from בית שמאי.

steps.title: Even בית שמאי agree the animal goes back to the flock
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say a הקדש made by mistake still counts. Even so, here they agree the animal is not holy, because it turned out the נזירות was not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't בית שמאי say that a הקדש made by mistake is still הקדש? Even so, once it becomes clear that his נזירות was not a proper vow, the animal goes out and grazes in the flock.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives his proof. Even the strict side, בית שמאי, let the animal go back to being ordinary in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי usually hold that making something holy by mistake still works. But once the vow is undone, it is clear the נזירות was never a proper vow from the start. So even בית שמאי say the animal goes out to the flock.

keyTerms.meaning: Making something holy by mistake
It became clear, looking back, that the matter was really so
It goes out and grazes in the flock. It is an ordinary animal, not holy

phrases.english: Don't Beit Shammai say
that consecration in error is consecration,
yet once the matter has become clear
that he did not vow properly,
phrases.notes: Once the חכם undid the vow, it is as if the נזירות was never properly made.

phrases.english: it goes out and grazes in the flock.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הֶקְדֵּשׁ בְּטָעוּת הָוֵי הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves רבי ירמיה's claim from step 7 by showing what בית שמאי hold.
steps.raayaObject: That the animal of a נזיר whose vow was undone is not holy
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה, which follows בית שמאי (הקדש בטעות הוי הקדש), still says the animal goes to the flock

steps.title: בית הלל agree too, because a תמורה falls away when the first הקדש falls away
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל say a תמורה made by mistake still counts. But that is only when the first הקדש stands. Here the first הקדש was uprooted, so any תמורה is uprooted too.
steps.simpleTranslation: For בית הלל too: even though they say a תמורה made by mistake is still a תמורה, that is only when the first הקדש is still there. But when the first הקדש is uprooted, the תמורה is uprooted too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה applies his lesson to בית הלל. He shows that their rule about a mistaken תמורה does not change the answer here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think בית הלל, who say a תמורה made by mistake counts, would hold the animal is still holy. רבי ירמיה explains that a תמורה can only stand on top of a real first הקדש. Once undoing the vow uproots the first הקדש, nothing is left for the תמורה to hold onto.

keyTerms.meaning: Swapping a holy animal for another animal. The new animal becomes holy too
The first, basic הקדש that everything else rests on
Was uprooted, cancelled from the start

steps.whatToRemember: When a חכם undoes a vow, the first הקדש is uprooted from the start. So everyone agrees the animal goes back to the flock, both בית שמאי and בית הלל, even though they hold that mistakes in הקדש or תמורה can count.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key difference: a mistake in making something holy is not the same as a holiness that was uprooted from its very start.

phrases.english: According to Beit Hillel as well,
even though they say
that a substitution made in error is a substitution,

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ לְעִיקַּר הֶקְדֵּשׁ.
phrases.english: that applies only where the original consecration still exists.
But where the original consecration is uprooted,
the substitution is uprooted as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבֵית הִלֵּל נָמֵי, אַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמְרִי תְּמוּרָה בְּטָעוּת הָוְיָא תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי ירמיה's point by applying the lesson from בית שמאי to בית הלל, and answers a possible objection from בית הלל's view on תמורה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Undoing the vow uproots the first הקדש, so the animal is ordinary according to everyone, and even a תמורה made from it falls away.

steps.title: Mistake versus purpose when labeling the tenth animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בית שמאי's line from the משנה about calling the ninth animal 'tenth', then brings an אמוראים dispute about it. רב נחמן says only a mistake makes it holy. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say a mistake does, and doing it on purpose does even more.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said in the משנה: 'Don't you agree that if he called the ninth animal tenth...' It was taught that there is a dispute about מעשר. רב נחמן says: only his mistake makes it holy, not his intention. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say: his mistake makes it holy, and all the more so his intention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line about מעשר בהמה and shows that the אמוראים argue over whether calling the wrong animal 'tenth' on purpose also makes it holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that if a person honestly mixes up the count and calls the ninth animal 'tenth', it becomes holy. The question is a person who knows it is the ninth and calls it 'tenth' anyway. רב נחמן says that does nothing. The other two say it works even better than a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said', a way of quoting a line from an earlier source so it can be discussed
Animal tithe: every tenth animal counted out of the pen becomes holy
His mistake, meaning he really thought it was the tenth
His intention, meaning he knew it was not the tenth and said 'tenth' on purpose
'It was stated', which introduces a dispute between אמוראים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix these up. 'Mistake' means he really thought it was the tenth. 'Intention' means he knew it was the ninth and labeled it 'tenth' anyway.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: He is quoting בית שמאי's words from the משנה.

phrases.english: Don't you agree
that if he called the ninth one 'tenth,' etc.
It was stated: regarding the tithe,
Rav Nachman said:
his mistake makes it holy, but not his intention.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna say:
his mistake makes it holy, and all the more so his intention.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of a נזיר whose vow was undone and goes back to an earlier line of the משנה to start a new discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן: only an honest mistake makes the ninth or eleventh animal holy as מעשר. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא: a mistake does, and a deliberate label does even more.

steps.title: רבא recalls בית שמאי's argument and בית הלל's silence
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins a challenge to רב נחמן. He recalls that בית שמאי asked בית הלל whether they agree that all three animals become holy, and בית הלל had no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: According to you, who say only his mistake counts and not his intention, think about what בית שמאי said to בית הלל: 'Don't you agree that if he called the ninth tenth, the tenth ninth, and the eleventh tenth, all three are holy?' And בית הלל were silent.
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up רבא's challenge. He reminds us that בית הלל had no reply to בית שמאי's proof from מעשר, and the actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי used מעשר to prove that a הקדש made by mistake still counts. The משנה says בית הלל stayed quiet, as if they had no answer. רבא will now ask why, if רב נחמן is right, בית הלל could not answer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to you', the start of a challenge to someone's own view
All three of them are holy
'And they were silent', meaning they had no answer

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
According to you, who said
his mistake, but not his intention,
consider what Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:
Don't you agree
that if he called the ninth one 'tenth,'
and the tenth one 'ninth,' and the eleventh one 'tenth,'
that all three are holy?
And Beit Hillel were silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an attack on רב נחמן's view from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that only a mistake makes מעשר holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: it recalls that בית הלל were silent. The point of the attack comes in step 12.

steps.title: בית הלל had an easy reply, so why didn't they use it?
steps.stepSummary: רבא's point: if רב נחמן is right, בית הלל could have told בית שמאי that מעשר is different, because it does not become holy on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them say to them: What about מעשר? It is different, since it does not become holy on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punch of רבא's challenge. According to רב נחמן, בית הלל had a simple answer to בית שמאי, so their silence is hard to explain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מעשר works only by mistake and not on purpose, then it is a strange kind of holiness. בית הלל could say we can't learn from it to regular הקדש, which works through clear intention. Since they stayed quiet, it seems no such answer existed, which goes against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let them say to them', a suggestion of a reply they should have given
'What about X, which has this feature?', pointing out that the source case is different
On purpose, deliberately

phrases.english: Let them say to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means בית הלל answering בית שמאי.

phrases.english: What about the tithe?
It is different, since it does not become holy on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge that step 11 set up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רב נחמן were right, בית הלל could have rejected the proof from מעשר by saying it is unusual. Their silence suggests they had no such reply.

steps.title: The reply would fail because of a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי defends רב נחמן. בית הלל could not give that reply, because a קל וחומר goes the other way: if מעשר, which doesn't work on purpose, still works by mistake, then הקדש, which does work on purpose, should surely work by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי said: This is the reason they did not say it to them, because there is a קל וחומר. If מעשר, which does not become holy on purpose, becomes holy by mistake, then הקדש, which does become holy on purpose, surely becomes holy by mistake too!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי answers רבא. He explains that בית הלל stayed quiet because the reply 'מעשר is different' would actually backfire on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The feature בית הלל would point to, that מעשר doesn't work on purpose, actually shows that מעשר is the weaker kind of holiness. If even the weaker kind takes hold by mistake, the stronger kind, הקדש, should certainly take hold by mistake. So the reply would only help בית שמאי, and רב נחמן's view stays standing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That is the reason', an explanation of something that was puzzling
Reasoning from a weaker case to a stronger one: if it is true in the weaker case, it is surely true in the stronger one
By mistake
'Is it not all the more so?', the end of a קל וחומר

steps.whatToRemember: רב שימי בר אשי defends רב נחמן: בית הלל could not answer 'מעשר is different', because that very difference would create a קל וחומר that a הקדש made by mistake should count. The next step rejects this קל וחומר.
steps.whyThisMatters: The step shows that a feature which looks like a reason to reject a proof can actually make the proof stronger.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi said:
This is the reason they did not say it to them,
because there is a kal vachomer:
If the tithe, which does not become holy on purpose,
becomes holy by mistake,
then consecration, which does become holy on purpose,
is it not all the more so?!
phrases.notes: He means that הקדש should surely become holy by mistake too.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּלָא אָמְרִי לְהוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from steps 11 and 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the suggested reply could not be used
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל's silence suggests that 'מעשר is different' was not a valid reply, which goes against רב נחמן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reply was not used because a קל וחומר would turn it into support for בית שמאי. So the silence does not disprove רב נחמן.

steps.title: The קל וחומר is rejected because הקדש depends on the owner's intention
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב שימי בר אשי's קל וחומר does not work. הקדש depends on the owner's intention, so it is not like מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so, because הקדש depends on the mind of its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the קל וחומר from the previous step. It says the comparison between מעשר and הקדש does not hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שימי בר אשי argued: if מעשר works by mistake, then הקדש should surely work by mistake. The גמרא answers that הקדש only happens through the owner's own intention, and a mistake is not real intention. מעשר is different, because it becomes holy just by being counted as the tenth, so the קל וחומר falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so: the גמרא's way of rejecting an argument
By the intention (mind) of its owner
Depends on, hangs on

steps.confusionAlert: The words וְלָא הִיא are not a new opinion from a named rabbi. This is the גמרא itself saying that the previous argument is wrong.
steps.whatToRemember: הקדש needs the owner's real intention, so a mistake cannot make it holy. מעשר becomes holy through counting, so it works differently, and you cannot learn one from the other with a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: But it is not so,
because consecration depends on the intention of its owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ בְּדַעְתָּא דְמָרֵיהּ תְּלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר that רב שימי בר אשי used to defend רב נחמן in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר from מעשר to הקדש offered in step 13.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison fails. הקדש depends on the owner's intention, which a mistake lacks. מעשר becomes holy through counting, not through intention.

steps.title: New משנה: the נזיר whose animal was stolen
steps.stepSummary: A man vowed to be a נזיר and found that the animal for his offerings had been stolen. If he vowed before the theft, he is a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone vowed to be a נזיר, went to bring his animal, and found that it had been stolen. If he made the vow before his animal was stolen, he is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It is about a man who made a נזירות vow and then discovered that his animal had been stolen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow was made while the animal was still there, so the theft happened only afterward. Something that happens later does not cancel a vow that was already made, so he remains a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין: our משנה
Made a vow to be a נזיר
His animal (here, the one he planned to use for his offerings)
It was stolen
He is a נזיר; the vow stands

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who vowed to be a nazirite,
and went to bring his animal,
and found that it was stolen.

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְנְבָה בְּהֶמְתּוֹ נָזַר —
phrases.english: If he vowed naziriteship before his animal was stolen,
he is a nazirite.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁנָּדַר בְּנָזִיר, וְהָלַךְ לְהָבִיא אֶת בְּהֶמְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous sugya has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If a person vowed to be a נזיר before his animal was stolen, the later theft does not cancel the vow, and he is a נזיר.
